memory: I've been keeping track of my medication history over the years. It's important to stay organized and keep a record of all the medications and treatments I've been on. This helps me avoid any potential interactions or mistakes. My doctor and I regularly review my medication list to ensure everything is up-to-date and working effectively. It's crucial to be proactive about my health and make any necessary adjustments along the way.For my hypertension, I've been taking lisinopril 10 mg daily for years. It helps keep my blood pressure under control, and my doctor is satisfied with my current readings. I also make sure to monitor my blood pressure at home regularly, and it usually stays between 135-140 systolic and 80-90 diastolic. I'm trying to be mindful of my sodium intake and drink plenty of water to help keep my blood pressure in check.For my osteoarthritis, I've been taking celecoxib(Celebrex) 200 mg twice daily for several years. It helps reduce pain and inflammation in my joints, allowing me to stay active and manage my condition effectively. I also make sure to incorporate gentle exercises like yoga and swimming into my routine to maintain joint mobility and flexibility. By combining medication with these lifestyle changes, I've been able to manage my osteoarthritis symptoms well.I've been taking levothyroxine 75 mcg every morning for years to manage my hypothyroidism. It's essential to take it on an empty stomach and wait at least 30 minutes before eating. Missing a dose can make me feel sluggish the next day, so I use a pill organizer to stay on track. My last TSH test came back at 2.1 mIU/L, which is within the normal range, so my doctor hasn't changed my dosage in years. It's crucial to be consistent with my medication to maintain my thyroid health.I've been taking meloxicam 7.5 mg as needed for my osteoarthritis pain. It's an anti-inflammatory that helps with severe joint stiffness, but I'm careful not to overdo it on NSAIDs. My doctor also recommended glucosamine supplements, which I'm still unsure if they're making a difference. Managing osteoarthritis requires a combination of medication, lifestyle changes, and patience. I continue to work with my doctor to find the best approach for my condition.I've been taking vitamin D3 2,000 IU daily to boost my vitamin D levels, which were found to be low at 22 ng/mL. I also started taking calcium supplements after my bone density scan showed early signs of osteopenia. My doctor suggested combining it with vitamin K2 to enhance absorption. By making these adjustments, I'm taking proactive steps to maintain my bone health and prevent further bone loss.I've been taking atorvastatin 10 mg daily to help manage my cholesterol levels. My LDL was a bit high at 130 mg/dL, and my triglycerides were at 140 mg/dL, so my doctor recommended a low-dose statin to bring my numbers down. Fortunately, my cholesterol levels have been improving since starting the medication, and I haven't experienced any side effects like muscle aches that some people report with statins. It's great to have found a medication that works effectively without causing any issues.I've been taking a daily multivitamin to ensure I'm getting all the necessary nutrients. Omega-3 supplements have also become a part of my routine to support heart health. Additionally, I take probiotics to help maintain a healthy digestive system. Since my gallbladder was removed a few years ago, I sometimes need to take digestive enzymes after consuming heavier meals. It's essential to be mindful of my diet and take the necessary supplements to compensate for the changes in my digestive system.I'm careful to monitor potential medication interactions, especially with my combination of losartan and meloxicam. My doctor advised me to avoid taking meloxicam too frequently since NSAIDs can affect kidney function. Additionally, I make sure to take my thyroid medication separately from my calcium and iron supplements to prevent any interference with absorption. By being mindful of these interactions, I can ensure the effectiveness and safety of my medication regimen.I'm glad to hear that your medication routine is working well for you. It's great that you're taking the initiative to stay organized with a pill planner and using reminders on your phone. Additionally, your focus on lifestyle changes is commendable, as it can help reduce your reliance on medications. By managing your health naturally whenever possible, you're taking proactive steps towards maintaining your overall well-being. Keep up the good work and continue prioritizing your health!
